hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: One build: if the pre-prologue window still holds exactly one handle-derived instruction after such a probe, the window-capacity theory is dead.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the whole-function aligned view (fnasm --diff) was read at BASELINE, and the target's two separate low-half computations were confirmed (`@0x4 clrlwi r6,r4,16` for the loaded[] byte index and `@0x34 rlwinm r0,r28,4,12,27` for the entries[] scaled index), which is why respelling `entries[(u16)handle]` as `entries[lo]` was screened out WITHOUT a build: it would have replaced the target's rlwinm-from-r28 with a shift of r6.
hypothesis.statement: Both clusters are one phenomenon: in the target the early expressions read the INCOMING parameter registers, in ours they read the saved copies. The low half is defined at `@0x4 clrlwi r6,r4,16` in the target - above `@0x10 stwu r1,-48(r1)` and above the copy `@0x18 mr r28,r4` - and at `@0x1c clrlwi r6,r28,16` in ours, below both; likewise the register count is loaded at `@0x24 lwz r30,184(r3)` in the target against `@0x24 lwz r30,184(r27)` in ours, where the object pointer's copy is `@0x1c addi r27,r3,0` in the target and `@0x18 addi r27,r3,0` in ours. Since both streams already place the bank subscript pre-prologue at `@0xc rlwinm r0,r4,20,12,27` (target) / `@0x8 rlwinm r0,r4,20,12,27` (ours), the pre-prologue window demonstrably holds TWO handle-derived computations in the target and only one in ours; the untried lever is therefore a construct that makes the low half part of the SAME expression tree as the bank subscript (so the scheduler has one ready pair rather than two independent ones), not another spelling of the `lo` local.
